newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian troops killed in heavy fighting.
newsitem.headline: Colombian troops killed in heavy fighting.

text.p: As many as 25 Colombian soldiers were killed and scores more wounded and reported missing in fierce fighting with leftist rebels in mountains just east of Bogota on Sunday, unnamed military sources told Colombian television.

The chief army spokeswoman was unable to confirm or deny the figures given in the TV Hoy news report, but said a number of soldiers were killed, injured or were missing in the battle near San Juanito about 30 miles (50 km) east of the capital.

If initial reports of the death toll are confirmed it will be the heaviest blow dealt to the army since rebels overran a military base in southern Colombia last August when they killed 27 soldiers and took 60 prisoners.

"There are soliders dead and others have been missing. But it is very difficult to get into the zone because of the intensity of the fighting and it is still too early to confirm any numbers," the spokeswoman told Reuters.
"Some troops are reported missing but we don't yet know if they have been captured or whether they have just taken cover," she added.
The battle broke out on Sunday morning when a 50-strong counterinsurgency unit came under fire from about 400 guerrillas of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), the spokeswoman said.
Fighting erupted shortly after the army unit rescued a Bogota businessman kidnapped by suspected guerrillas on Jan. 30.

The spokeswoman added that the FARC contingent was thought to be an elite force in charge of guarding the guerrilla army's general secretariat, including its supreme commander Manuel Marulanda, alias "Sureshot".

Army helicopters carrying reinforcements came under fire and were forced to drop 160 troops miles (kilometres) from the fighting and leave them to make their way on foot through treacherous terrain to the battle zone.
"As we flew helicopters into the battle zone, we came under fire. Two were hit, one pilot was injured and a soldier died," Gen. Juan Santos told TV Hoy.
TV Hoy, citing unnamed top-ranking officers, said 25 soldiers were killed and at least 15 taken prisoner.
